questions.question_text: Given $f(x) = 4x - 9$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{x + 9}{4}$, what is the fully simplified result of the composite expression $f(g(x))$?

options.why: Subtracted $9$ without cancelling the constant term after expansion.
Divided the outer term by $4$ incorrectly during simplification.
Added the constants $+9$ and $+9$ instead of subtracting the outer $-9$.

questions.question_text: For $f(x) = 7 - 3x$, which function $g(x)$ satisfies both $f(g(x)) = x$ and $g(f(x)) = x$?

options.why: Changed the sign of the constant term $7$ incorrectly.
Ignored the negative coefficient of $x$ when rearranging for the inverse.
Multiplied by $3$ instead of dividing by the coefficient $3$.

questions.solution_text:
$x = 7 - 3y \implies 3y = 7 - x \implies g(x) = \dfrac{7 - x}{3}$
$f(g(x)) = 7 - 3\left(\dfrac{7 - x}{3}\right) = 7 - (7 - x) = x$

questions.question_text: For $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x + 5}$ ($x \ne -5$), which function $g(x)$ is verified as the inverse by $f(g(x)) = x$?

options.why: Added $5$ instead of subtracting $5$ when isolating the inverse variable.
Omitted the reciprocal operation $\dfrac{1}{x}$ when inverting the rational function.
Placed $-5$ in the denominator instead of subtracting from the whole fraction.

questions.question_text: For the rational function $f(x) = \dfrac{x - 2}{x + 3}$, which function $g(x)$ satisfies $(f \circ g)(x) = x$?

options.why: Took the reciprocal $\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$ instead of finding the inverse function.
Made sign errors when collecting terms in $x(y + 3) = y - 2$.
Failed to factor out common terms correctly in the numerator.

questions.solution_text: $x = \dfrac{y - 2}{y + 3} \implies x(y + 3) = y - 2 \implies xy + 3x = y - 2 \implies y(1 - x) = 3x + 2 \implies g(x) = \dfrac{3x + 2}{1 - x}$

questions.question_text: Given $f(x) = x^3 - 5$, what is the result of substituting $g(x) = \sqrt[3]{x + 5}$ into $f(x)$?

options.why: Added $5$ twice instead of cancelling $+5$ with $-5$.
Did not cancel the constant term under the radical with the outer constant.
Cubed the variable but failed to apply the power to the radical expression.

questions.question_text: Given $f(x) = \sqrt{2x + 6}$ for $x \ge -3$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 6}{2}$ for $x \ge 0$, on what domain does the identity $g(f(x)) = x$ hold?

options.why: Used the domain of $g(x)$ instead of the inner function's domain $x \ge -3$.
Used the wrong sign for the endpoint of the radical function.
Ignored the square root domain restriction requiring $2x + 6 \ge 0$.

questions.solution_text: The composite $g(f(x))$ is defined for all $x$ in the domain of $f(x)$, which requires $2x + 6 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -3$.

questions.question_text: If $f(x) = 5x^3 + 2$ and $g(x) = f^{-1}(x)$, what is the exact value of $f(g(42)) + g(f(-8))$?

options.why: Subtracted $-8$ as $+8$, giving $42 + 8 = 50$ instead of $42 + (-8) = 34$.
Assumed the two inverse evaluations cancel each other out.
Multiplied the inputs $42 \times 8$ rather than adding the outputs.

questions.question_text: For the invertible function $f(x) = \dfrac{3x + 1}{x - 2}$ ($x \ne 2$), evaluate the composite expression $(f \circ f^{-1})(17)$.

options.why: Substituted $17$ into $f(x)$ directly rather than evaluating the identity $f(f^{-1}(17))$.
Substituted $17$ into $f^{-1}(x)$ directly instead of simplifying the composition.
Assumed the composition evaluates to zero.

questions.question_text: A student tests $f(x) = x^4$ and $g(x) = \sqrt[4]{x}$ and computes $f(g(x)) = (\sqrt[4]{x})^4 = x$. Why does this NOT prove that $g$ is the inverse of $f$ on $(-\infty, \infty)$?

options.text: Because $g(f(x)) = \sqrt[4]{x^4} = |x| \ne x$ for negative numbers, and $\sqrt[4]{x}$ is undefined for $x < 0$.
Because the composition $f(g(x))$ should have simplified to $x^4$ instead of $x$.
options.why: Incorrectly claimed the algebra in $f(g(x))$ was wrong.

options.text: Because $x^4$ is an odd function that has no inverse on any domain.
options.why: Incorrectly classified $x^4$ as an odd function instead of an even function.

options.text: Because inverse functions can only be verified by comparing graphs, not by algebra.
options.why: Denied the mathematical validity of algebraic composition verification.

questions.solution_text:
For $x < 0$, $g(f(x)) = \sqrt[4]{x^4} = |x| = -x \ne x$.
$f(x) = x^4$ is not one-to-one on $(-\infty, \infty)$, so both compositions must be tested on the appropriate domain.

questions.question_text: For the restricted function $f(x) = 1 - \sqrt{x}$ ($x \ge 0$) and its proposed inverse $f^{-1}(x) = (1 - x)^2$, on what domain of $x$ does the identity $f^{-1}(f(x)) = x$ hold?

options.why: Used the domain of $f^{-1}(x)$ instead of the domain of the inner function $f(x)$.
Ignored the square root domain restriction $x \ge 0$ on the inner function.
Confused the condition $1 - \sqrt{x} \le 0$ with the domain of $f$.

questions.solution_text:
$f^{-1}(f(x)) = (1 - (1 - \sqrt{x}))^2 = (\sqrt{x})^2 = x$
This identity requires $x \ge 0$ so that $\sqrt{x}$ is a real number.
